data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The safest protocol is deterministic replay from the last durable barrier, treating any workspace without a terminal record as unverified and requiring replay-to-barrier before any reclamation decision.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The barrier log itself may be incomplete or corrupted by the crash, making replay non-deterministic or impossible.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Replay cost may be prohibitive for large workspaces, rendering the protocol practically unusable despite its theoretical safety.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Hidden non-deterministic inputs such as wall-clock time or entropy drawn between barriers may not be captured, causing replay divergence.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The protocol records monotonic barrier logs of workspace state transitions. A crash with no terminal record implies the final epoch is uncommitted. Reclamation mandates replaying the deterministic computation from the last committed barrier to reconstitute the workspace, comparing its output against a recorded content hash, and only then deciding whether evidence was completed. The durably recorded artifacts are barrier epoch markers, deterministic state digests at each barrier, and the content hash of the completed evidence set.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
